To faint; to become unconscious.

examples.text: I pass out at the sight of blood.
I passed out on the train after drinking a bottle of vodka.
At the end of the presentations, the whole folk scene joined hands and sang We Shall Overcome so many times that everybody passed out.

glosses: To fall asleep, usually as a result of drunkenness or the consumption of drugs.
To distribute.

examples.text: We'll pass out copies of the agenda.

glosses: To graduate, usually marked by a ceremony at the end of training.

examples.text: He wasn't allowed to finish his training to go to France; but was sent to England on a Physical Training Course and passed out First Class.

"She had asked at Paddington for a return to Lympstone on the Exmouth branch, where her son was due to pass out as a Royal Marine that afternoon, at the local training camp.

glosses: To become proficient in a particular job or task.

examples.text: "It took me about a month to pass out on this box," he adds. glosses: Lacking courage, spirit, or energy; cowardly; dejected.

glosses: Barely perceptible; not bright, or loud, or sharp.

examples.text: There was a faint red light in the distance.

glosses: Slight; minimal.

examples.text: do you have the faintest understanding of what they mean?

glosses: Sickly, so as to make a person feel faint.

examples.text: Happening to pass a fruiterer’s on their way; the door of which was open, though the shop was by this time shut; one of them remarked how faint the peaches smelled.

glosses: The act of fainting, syncope.

examples.text: She suffered another faint.

glosses: The state of one who has fainted; a swoon.

To lose consciousness through a lack of oxygen or nutrients to the brain, usually as a result of suddenly reduced blood flow (may be caused by emotional trauma, loss of blood or various medical conditions).

examples.text: If I send them away fasting […] they will faint by the way.

examples.text: If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is small.
